root_idea.summary: The root centers on deliberately tracking, pursuing, and seeking something.
root_idea.development: This orientation extends to repeated or gradual inquiry, listening out for voices, and the hostile tracking and divulgence of speech. Related classical forms also describe a persistent seeker or a guide by night.

qac_form_accounting.reason: Displayed under the normalized singular citation form قِسِّيسٌ; the supplied Quran occurrence is its plural form.

senses.definition: A learned and devout Christian, especially one of the religious leaders or priests.
senses.usage_conditions: The Quran occurrence is the plural قِسِّيسِينَ, used of Christian religious figures in a religious context.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To seek after or pursue something repeatedly, gradually, or deliberately.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A transitive verb, including the pursuit of news or tidings.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To calumniate, maliciously misrepresent, or spread evil speech about people.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Includes speaking against people behind their backs or in their absence, and harming or annoying them by foul speech.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To search out and consume the meat on a bone, leaving none, and extract its marrow; also, to eat what is on a table.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized use for painstakingly picking through food.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become a قَسّ or قِسِّيس, or to attain the rank or office of one.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A verbal use distinct from the noun naming the Christian religious figure.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To listen for or endeavor to hear voices.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Attested in the construction تَقَسَّسَ أَصْوَاتَ القَوْمِ بِاللَّيْلِ, listening by night.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To seek what one might eat, or seek food.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Recorded in a description of a lion; the animal is an illustrative context, not an exclusive restriction.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To ask or inquire about the affairs of others.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A conventional inquiry into other people's affairs.

other_classical_meanings.definition: An intelligent, ingenious, clever, or learned man.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A broader reported application of the headword apart from its Christian religious title.
Reported in the expression سَيْرٌ قَسِيسٌ, a diligent or persistent journey.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A type of cloth or garment made of flax mixed with silk.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A technical textile term; reports differ about its geographic association and etymology.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A calumniator or slanderer; one who pries into news and maliciously divulges it.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The divulged information is described as capable of causing discord or dissension.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A persistent or leisurely seeker; an inquirer into other people's affairs; a guide by night.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The forms are used for deliberate seeking and, in one reported usage, for a person who guides by night.
A reported usage described as outside the principal semantic branch.
Reported on the authority of al-Shaybānī, with the lexical attribution explicitly treated as anomalous or uncertain.
An idiomatic verbal construction with بِالْكَلْبِ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Bad or inferior, used of a coin.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Reported in دِرْهَمٌ قَسِيٌّ, but its attribution to this root is disputed; it may be a Persian term or an inflected form of قَاسٌّ.

lane_unit_coverage.note: The primary seeking or pursuing sense is represented.
The calumny and malicious speech branch is represented.
The specialized pursuit and consumption of meat is represented.
The verbal sense of becoming or attaining the office of a qass/qissis is represented.
Listening for voices by night is represented.
The seeking of food is represented.
Inquiry into others' affairs is represented.
The Christian religious title and the broader learned-man application are both represented.
The calumniating and maliciously divulging person is represented.
The persistent or leisurely seeker is represented.
The inquirer into others' affairs is represented under the same lexical branch.

cautions: The sole Quran occurrence is the plural قِسِّيسِينَ; the public headword is normalized to the singular citation form قِسِّيسٌ.
The tracking and seeking material explains the root's semantic orientation and related classical derivatives; it is not an additional Quranic sense of قِسِّيسِينَ.
The textile term قَسِّيٌّ has competing reports concerning its origin and geographic association.
unassigned_or_ambiguous_evidence: A root-level discussion records قُسَاسٌ as a place-name and قَسَاسِيَّةٌ as a nisba for swords; this is geographic and derivational information rather than a confidently assignable independent lexical meaning of the root.
